questions.title: Basic Java Program
questions.objective: Write the smallest complete Java program: a class named Main with a main() method that prints one line.
questions.problem_statement: Task: Write a Java program using a class named Main and the standard main() method. Display the message Java is ready using System.out.println().
questions.output_format: A single line: Java is ready
hints: Every Java program needs a class; here it must be named Main.
Execution starts in public static void main(String[] args).
Inside main(), call System.out.println("Java is ready");

extra_fields.output_format: A single line: Java is ready

questions.title: Multiple Output Statements
questions.objective: Use several println() statements and observe that each one prints on a new line.
questions.problem_statement: Task: Write a Java program that displays three predefined messages on separate lines using three System.out.println() statements. Print Learn Java, Practice Daily, and Build Projects in the given order.
questions.output_format:
Three lines:
Learn Java
Practice Daily
Build Projects
sample_outputs:
Learn Java
Practice Daily
Build Projects
hints: println() moves the cursor to the next line after printing.
Statements in main() run from top to bottom, so order matters.
Write three println() statements, one for each message, in the given order.

test_cases.output:
Learn Java
Practice Daily
Build Projects

extra_fields.output_format:
Three lines:
Learn Java
Practice Daily
Build Projects

questions.title: Print Without a Line Break
questions.objective: Understand the difference between print() and println() by joining two outputs on one line.
questions.problem_statement: Task: Write a Java program that displays Code and Mentor on the same line using two System.out.print() statements. Do not include a space between the words.
questions.output_format: A single line: CodeMentor
hints: print() does not add a newline after the text, while println() does.
Do not put a space at the end of "Code" or the start of "Mentor".
Use System.out.print("Code"); followed by System.out.print("Mentor");

extra_fields.output_format: A single line: CodeMentor

questions.title: Comment Types
questions.objective: Use all three Java comment styles in one program and confirm that none of them appear in the output.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that uses all three kinds of Java comments:
- A documentation comment (/** ... */) directly above the class declaration.
- A block comment (/* ... */) inside the main() method.
- A single-line comment (// ...) inside the main() method.

The program must display the following three lines and nothing else:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added

Comments are ignored by the compiler, so none of the comment text should appear in the output.
questions.output_format:
Three lines:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added
sample_outputs:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added
hints: A single-line comment starts with // and ends at the end of the line.
A block comment starts with /* and ends with */; a documentation comment starts with /** and ends with */.
Place the /** */ comment above public class Main, put the other two comments inside main(), and add three println() statements.

test_cases.output:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added

extra_fields.output_format:
Three lines:
Single-line comment added
Block comment added
Documentation comment added

questions.title: Print Quotation Marks
questions.objective: Use the \" escape sequence to print double quotation marks inside a String literal.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that displays the following line exactly, including the double quotation marks:
She said "Java is fun"

A double quote normally ends a String literal, so you need an escape sequence to print it.
questions.output_format: A single line: She said "Java is fun"
hints: Writing "She said "Java is fun"" causes a compile error because the second quote ends the String.
The escape sequence \" prints a double quotation mark.
Use System.out.println("She said \"Java is fun\"");

extra_fields.output_format: A single line: She said "Java is fun"

questions.title: Print a Windows Path
questions.objective: Use the \\ escape sequence to print a backslash character.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that displays the following Windows folder path exactly:
C:\Program Files\Java\bin

In a Java String literal, a single backslash starts an escape sequence, so you need a special sequence to print one backslash.
questions.output_format: A single line: C:\Program Files\Java\bin
hints: A single \ followed by a letter is treated as an escape sequence, and \P or \J causes a compile error.
The escape sequence \\ prints one backslash.
Use System.out.println("C:\\Program Files\\Java\\bin");

extra_fields.output_format: A single line: C:\Program Files\Java\bin

questions.title: Tab-Aligned Header
questions.objective: Use the \t escape sequence to separate values with tab characters.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that displays a two-line table. Separate the values on each line with a single tab character, not spaces.

Line 1: Name, Dept, and Year
Line 2: Alex, CSE, and 2026

Each line should have exactly one tab between neighbouring values and no tab at the beginning or end.
questions.output_format:
Two lines:
Name<TAB>Dept<TAB>Year
Alex<TAB>CSE<TAB>2026
where <TAB> is a single tab character.
hints: The escape sequence \t inserts a tab character.
Spaces and tabs look similar on screen but are different characters, so the judge treats them differently.
Use System.out.println("Name\tDept\tYear"); and a similar statement for the second line.

extra_fields.output_format:
Two lines:
Name<TAB>Dept<TAB>Year
Alex<TAB>CSE<TAB>2026
where <TAB> is a single tab character.

questions.title: Read a Full Name
questions.objective: Read one complete line, including spaces, with Scanner.nextLine() and print it unchanged.
questions.problem_statement: Task: Write a Java program that reads one complete line of text using Scanner.nextLine() and displays it unchanged. The input may contain multiple words separated by spaces.
questions.input_format: A single line containing a full name.
questions.output_format: The name exactly as entered.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of name <= 100
The name does not begin or end with a space.
hints: Import Scanner with import java.util.Scanner; at the top of the file.
Create it with Scanner sc = new Scanner(System.in);
Read the line with sc.nextLine() and print it with System.out.println().

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing a full name.
extra_fields.output_format: The name exactly as entered.

questions.title: Personalized Greeting
questions.objective: Join fixed text and an input value into one output line using the + operator.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that reads a person's full name and displays a greeting in this exact format:
Hello, <name>! Welcome to Java.

Replace <name> with the name that was read. Keep the comma, the space after it, the exclamation mark, and the final full stop exactly as shown.
questions.input_format: A single line containing a full name.
questions.output_format: A single line: Hello, <name>! Welcome to Java.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of name <= 50
The name does not begin or end with a space.
sample_outputs: Hello, Alex Morgan! Welcome to Java.
hints: Read the full name with nextLine(), since it can contain spaces.
The + operator joins Strings: "Hello, " + name produces one combined String.
Print "Hello, " + name + "! Welcome to Java." with System.out.println().

test_cases.output: Hello, Alex Morgan! Welcome to Java.
Hello, Ravi Kumar! Welcome to Java.
Hello, Mohammed Abdul Rahman! Welcome to Java.
Hello, Sneha P. Iyer! Welcome to Java.
Hello, Ananya Rao! Welcome to Java.
Hello, Jean-Luc Picard! Welcome to Java.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing a full name.
extra_fields.output_format: A single line: Hello, <name>! Welcome to Java.

questions.title: Prompt and Read Input
questions.objective: Combine print() for a prompt with Scanner input and println() for output on the same line.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that displays the prompt Enter your city: (followed by one space) using System.out.print(). Then read one complete line from standard input and display the entered city using System.out.println().

Because print() does not add a newline, the city appears on the same line as the prompt. For automated judging, the input you type is not shown in the output, so the expected output is the prompt followed directly by the city that your program prints.
questions.input_format: A single line containing a city name (may contain spaces).
questions.output_format: A single line: Enter your city: followed by one space and the city name.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of city name <= 50
The city name does not begin or end with a space.
hints: System.out.print("Enter your city: ") prints the prompt and keeps the cursor on the same line.
Remember the single space after the colon inside the prompt string.
Read the city with nextLine() and print it with System.out.println(city).

test_cases.output: Enter your city: Rio de Janeiro

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing a city name (may contain spaces).
extra_fields.output_format: A single line: Enter your city: followed by one space and the city name.

questions.title: Preserve an Empty Input Line
questions.objective: Recognise that nextLine() returns an empty String for a blank line and that blank lines must still be printed.
questions.problem_statement: Task: Write a Java program that reads exactly three lines and displays them in the same order. The second line may be empty. Do not skip the empty line or replace it with text.
questions.input_format: Three lines. The second line may be empty.
questions.output_format: The same three lines in the same order, including an empty second line if present.
questions.constraints:
0 <= length of line 2 <= 100
1 <= length of lines 1 and 3 <= 100
hints: An empty line is still a line; nextLine() returns "" for it.
Printing an empty String with println() produces a blank line.
Read three lines with nextLine() and print all three, without checking whether any is empty.

test_cases.input:
Top
Middle line with spaces
Bottom
test_cases.output:
Top
Middle line with spaces
Bottom

extra_fields.input_format: Three lines. The second line may be empty.
extra_fields.output_format: The same three lines in the same order, including an empty second line if present.

questions.title: Read Word by Word
questions.objective: Use Scanner.next() to read individual words (tokens) and see how it skips over spaces.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that reads one line containing exactly three words and displays each word on its own line, in the same order.

The words may be separated by one or more spaces. Use Scanner.next(), which reads one word at a time and skips any spaces before it.
questions.input_format: A single line containing exactly three words separated by one or more spaces.
questions.output_format: Three lines, each containing one word, in the original order.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of each word <= 20
Words contain no spaces.
hints: next() returns the next word and automatically skips the spaces in between.
Calling next() three times gives you the three words in order.
Print each word with its own System.out.println() statement.

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing exactly three words separated by one or more spaces.
extra_fields.output_format: Three lines, each containing one word, in the original order.

questions.title: Reverse Line Order

questions.problem_statement:

Each line must be printed exactly as it was read.

Print third, then second, then first.

questions.title: Print Java Source Text
questions.objective: Combine the \" and \\ escape sequences to print text that itself contains Java escape sequences.
questions.output_format: A single line: System.out.println("Hello\nWorld");
hints: You need \" for each quotation mark and \\ for the backslash.
If you write \n alone inside your String, Java prints a real line break instead of the two characters.
Build the literal piece by piece: "System.out.println(\"Hello\\nWorld\");"

extra_fields.output_format: A single line: System.out.println("Hello\nWorld");

questions.title: Commented-Out Code
questions.objective: Disable a line of code by turning it into a comment, a common technique while debugging.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that contains three System.out.println() statements, which print Step 1: Start, Step 2: Debug, and Step 3: Finish in that order.

Disable the statement that prints Step 2: Debug by turning it into a single-line comment (//) instead of deleting it. When the program runs, it must display only the first and third lines.
questions.output_format:
Two lines:
Step 1: Start
Step 3: Finish
hints: A line that starts with // is ignored by the compiler.
Find the println() statement that prints Step 2: Debug.
Put // at the start of that statement and leave the other two unchanged.

extra_fields.output_format:
Two lines:
Step 1: Start
Step 3: Finish

questions.title: Correct Main Method Declaration
questions.objective: Identify the parts of the main method signature that the JVM requires and fix an incorrect declaration.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A beginner declared the program's entry point as public void Main(String args). The program compiles, but the JVM cannot run it because this is not a valid entry point. The declaration has three mistakes.

Write the program using the correct standard entry point public static void main(String[] args), and display Execution started.
questions.output_format: A single line: Execution started
hints: Compare public void Main(String args) with public static void main(String[] args) word by word.
Java is case-sensitive, so Main and main are different names.
Add static, rename Main to main, and change String args to String[] args.

extra_fields.output_format: A single line: Execution started

questions.title: Repair a Program with Three Errors
questions.objective: Read compiler errors and fix several different syntax mistakes in one program.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A beginner wrote a program that should display Program repaired and All errors fixed on two separate lines, but the program does not compile because of three errors:
- In the first print statement, System is written as system.
- The first print statement is missing its semicolon.
- The text in the second print statement is missing its closing double quotation mark.

Write the corrected program so that it compiles and displays both lines.

This is a source-code correction exercise, not a program that reads code from standard input.
questions.output_format:
Two lines:
Program repaired
All errors fixed
hints: Java is case-sensitive, and the class is called System with a capital S.
Every statement must end with a semicolon.
Every String literal needs both an opening and a closing double quotation mark.

extra_fields.output_format:
Two lines:
Program repaired
All errors fixed

questions.title: Correct Scanner Line Input
questions.objective: Diagnose why next() reads only one word and fix the program by switching to nextLine().
questions.problem_statement:
Task: A beginner program reads a sentence with Scanner.next() and prints it, but only the first word of the sentence appears in the output. This happens because next() reads only the next token and stops at the first space.

Correct the program so it uses Scanner.nextLine() instead, reads the complete sentence from standard input, and displays it unchanged.
questions.input_format: A single line containing a sentence.
questions.output_format: The sentence exactly as entered.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of sentence <= 200
The sentence does not begin or end with a space.
sample_inputs: Scanner reads input from the keyboard
sample_outputs: Scanner reads input from the keyboard
hints: With next(), the input Java supports object oriented programming prints only Java.
next() stops reading at whitespace, while nextLine() reads until the end of the line.
Change sc.next() to sc.nextLine() and keep the rest of the program the same.

test_cases.input: Scanner reads input from the keyboard
test_cases.output: Scanner reads input from the keyboard

test_cases.input: next() stops at the first space!
test_cases.output: next() stops at the first space!

test_cases.input: Strings, numbers, and symbols: all fine
test_cases.output: Strings, numbers, and symbols: all fine

extra_fields.input_format: A single line containing a sentence.
extra_fields.output_format: The sentence exactly as entered.

questions.title: Student Profile Card
questions.objective: Combine line input, String joining, and the \t and \" escape sequences to produce precisely formatted output.
questions.problem_statement:
Task: Write a Java program that reads a student's name, course name, and city on three separate lines and displays a profile card in this exact format:

STUDENT PROFILE
Name:<TAB><name>
Course:<TAB>"<course>"
City:<TAB><city>

Rules:
- <TAB> is a single tab character, not spaces.
- The course name must be surrounded by double quotation marks.
- Replace <name>, <course>, and <city> with the values that were read.
questions.input_format:
Three lines:
Line 1: student name
Line 2: course name
Line 3: city
questions.output_format: Four lines: the heading STUDENT PROFILE, then the Name, Course, and City lines in the format shown.
questions.constraints:
1 <= length of each line <= 60
No line is empty, and no line begins or ends with a space.
sample_outputs:
STUDENT PROFILE
Name:	Alex Morgan
Course:	"Java Fundamentals"
City:	Hyderabad

STUDENT PROFILE
Name:	Ananya Rao
Course:	"Data Analytics"
City:	Warangal
hints: Read all three values with nextLine(), because each can contain spaces.
Use \t for the tab and \" for each quotation mark inside String literals.
For the course line, print "Course:\t\"" + course + "\"".
